Shuffle a deck long enough, and its order is gone for good.
Inside a quantum computer, that chaos is the enemy.
Qubits are fragile. Heat and tiny flaws pile up, until answers can't be trusted.
So Rutgers and IBM staged a tug of war, across a hundred qubits.
One move scrambles neighbours, like a shuffle. The other checks a qubit, and resets it.
Nearly five thousand of each, on IBM's Heron processor.
Scramble more than half the time, and chaos wins.
Reset more often, and the whole system snaps into order.
Right at fifty-fifty, one nudge flips everything, like water turning to ice.
It's a step toward fault-tolerant quantum computers. Nobody has built one yet. Latoon. Voyaging the unseen. Follow for more.
